newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ wool prices mixed at Christchurch, Napier sales.
newsitem.headline: NZ wool prices mixed at Christchurch, Napier sales.

text.p: Prices for strong Crossbred wools eased, while prices for fine Crossbreds, Halfbreds and Merinos rose at Thursday's sales in Christchurch and Napier, Wools of New Zealand said.
The provisional market indicator was down four cents to 440, with fine up 45 to 915, medium up 14 to 548, strong down 10 to 378, and lamb down nine to 386.
On offer was 4,131 clean tonnes in 35,005 bales, chiefly comprising 40 percent crossbred fleece, 21 percent lambswool and 21 percent second shear. Passings amounted to 35.7 percent.

Compared with last week, all merino fleece was dearer. Halfbred fleece was 3-5 percent dearer. Crossbred fleece 32 and 34 micron was two percent dearer, while 35/36 micron was up to 2.5-5 percent cheaper and 37 micron and stronger was up to 3.0 percent cheaper.

Cotts was 5.0 percent cheaper and second shear was up to 3.0 percent cheaper. First lambs were cheaper, second lambs mixed, bulky skirtings generally unchanged and second shear bellies and pieces were 2-4 percent dearer. Major buying interest came from Western Europe, China and the local mills. The next sale is at Christchurch on March 13. --Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
